title: Codex usage limits
description: Decoded fields of codex:limits v1, a central Redis HASH with no TTL (CD-33). Redis transports every value as a string. Map windows by window_minutes (300 and 10080) regardless of their upstream slot. Publish the required fields together. The observation stamp and cadence govern freshness.

five_hour_none.description: 1 when the source confirms no 300-minute window; 0 when it reports that window. With 1, write both five-hour fields as zero in the same HSET. A missing or unreadable sample is not evidence of no window.

five_hour_pct.description: Used percent for the 300-minute window. Zero when five_hour_none is 1.

five_hour_resets_at.description: Unix seconds for the 300-minute reset. Zero means unknown or no window; use five_hour_none to distinguish absence.

seven_day_resets_at.description: Unix seconds for the 10080-minute reset. Zero means unknown.

updated_at.description: Unix seconds when the sample was observed. Republishing a cached sample must not advance this stamp.

expected_refresh_s.description: Seconds between expected fresh observations. Readers add their grace interval to this cadence.

host.description: Host where the observation was made.

source.description: Observation provenance. The rollout publisher writes rollout.

ts.description: Publish time in Unix seconds, stamped by the publisher wrapper when absent. Freshness uses updated_at.

plan_type.description: Optional upstream plan label for display. Derive window assignments from duration even when this field is present.

x-counterexamples.why: A plan with no five-hour window must declare it explicitly.
Upstream slot names cannot substitute for the duration-based fields.
The absence flag is a decoded integer.
Hash strings must be decoded before validation.
Readers need a positive observation cadence.
